Christopher Walken's 10 Best Movies, Ranked

8 March 2024 · RewindZone Archive

Trying to narrow down Christopher Walken's best movies can be a daunting task for any movie buff. With a career spanning over six decades and a diverse range of roles, it's challenging to decide which performances truly stand out among the rest.

Walken's unique acting style, characterised by his distinctive voice and mannerisms, has made him a cultural icon. From his early days in iconic films like "Annie Hall" and "The Deer Hunter" to his more recent appearances in blockbusters like "Catch Me If You Can" and "Hairspray," his performances have left their mark on cinema. However, with so many incredible roles under his belt, it's a tough choice to rank his very best.

In this article, we'll take a deep dive into Christopher Walken's illustrious career, analysing his most iconic roles and performances. We'll rank his top 10 movies, taking into account the impact of his characters, the critical acclaim, and the lasting cultural significance of each film.

Quick Fire Facts on Christopher Walken

  • Christopher Walken was born Ronald Walken on March 31, 1943, in Queens, New York.
  • He is known for intense and eccentric performances that have earned him critical acclaim and popularity.
  • Walken won an Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for his role in "The Deer Hunter" in 1978.
  • He started his career as a child actor and later transitioned to theater and film under the stage name Christopher Walken.
  • Walken has appeared in over 100 films and is known for his unique speaking style influenced by his upbringing in Queens with immigrant parents.
  • Despite his successful acting career, he has never turned down a role and believes that every movie experience is rewarding.

10. Seven Psychopaths (2012)

Advertisement

Director: Martin McDonagh

Main Cast: Colin Farrell, Sam Rockwell, Woody Harrelson, Christopher Walken

In this darkly comedic crime thriller, Walken shines as Hans, a seemingly harmless older man with a penchant for storytelling. His understated yet captivating performance adds depth and intrigue to the film's meta-narrative, showcasing his ability to seamlessly blend humour and pathos.

9. King of New York (1990)

Director: Abel Ferrara

Main Cast: Christopher Walken, Laurence Fishburne, David Caruso

Walken commands the screen as Frank White, a ruthless crime boss who seeks to reclaim his power after being released from prison. His portrayal of a complex antihero is both chilling and magnetic, solidifying his status as a master of intensity and nuance.

8. Antz (1998)

Director: Eric Darnell, Lawrence Guterman

Main Cast: Woody Allen, Sharon Stone, Jennifer Lopez, Christopher Walken (voice)

In this animated comedy, Walken lends his distinctive voice to the character of Colonel Cutter, an imposing ant soldier. Despite the film's lighthearted nature, Walken's commanding presence and deadpan delivery inject a layer of humour and depth into the character, showcasing his versatility as a voice actor.

7. Hairspray (2007)

Director: Adam Shankman

Main Cast: Nikki Blonsky, John Travolta, Michelle Pfeiffer, Christopher Walken

Walken's turn as Wilbur Turnblad, the endearing and supportive father figure, is a delightful departure from his typical intense roles. His infectious energy and willingness to embrace the film's campy spirit make his performance stand out, reminding audiences of his remarkable range as an actor.

6. The Addiction (1995)

Director: Abel Ferrara

Main Cast: Lili Taylor, Christopher Walken, Annabella Sciorra

In this unconventional horror film, Walken portrays a philosophical vampire who imparts wisdom and guidance to the newly-turned Kathleen (Lili Taylor). His portrayal is equal parts eerie and mesmerising, showcasing his ability to elevate even the most offbeat material with his remarkable presence.

5. Batman Returns (1992)

Director: Tim Burton

Main Cast: Michael Keaton, Danny DeVito, Michelle Pfeiffer, Christopher Walken

As the villainous Max Shreck, Walken delivers a deliciously wicked performance that perfectly complements the film's Gothic aesthetic. His portrayal of a corrupt and power-hungry businessman is both captivating and chilling, cementing his status as a master of villainy.

BONUS PICKS:

  • The Prophecy (1995)
  • Blast from the Past (1999)
  • Annie Hall (1973)
  • Heaven's Gate (1980)

4. True Romance (1993)

Director: Tony Scott

Main Cast: Christian Slater, Patricia Arquette, Dennis Hopper, Christopher Walken

In Quentin Tarantino's electrifying script, Walken steals every scene as the unforgettable Vincenzo Coccotti, a mob enforcer with a penchant for monologues. His iconic "Sicilian Scene" remains a cinematic masterpiece, showcasing his ability to captivate audiences with his commanding presence and impeccable delivery.

3. The Dead Zone (1983)

Director: David Cronenberg

Main Cast: Christopher Walken, Brooke Adams, Tom Skerritt

Walken's performance as Johnny Smith, a man haunted by visions of the future, is a tour de force. His ability to convey the character's internal struggle and moral dilemma is both haunting and deeply compelling, solidifying his status as a master of dramatic acting.

2. Catch Me If You Can (2002)

Director: Steven Spielberg

Main Cast: Leonardo DiCaprio, Tom Hanks, Christopher Walken

In this Steven Spielberg classic, Walken delivers a standout performance as Frank Abagnale Sr., the father of the con artist protagonist. His portrayal is a masterclass in subtlety and emotional depth, perfectly capturing the complex dynamics of a fractured family.

1. The Deer Hunter (1978)

Director: Michael Cimino

Main Cast: Robert De Niro, Christopher Walken, Meryl Streep

Walken's Oscar-winning performance as Nick Chevotarevich in this powerful war drama is nothing short of legendary. His portrayal of a soldier grappling with the trauma of war is both harrowing and deeply moving, cementing his status as one of the finest actors of his generation.

There you have it, fellow cinephiles—a countdown of Christopher Walken's most iconic and unforgettable performances. From his early dramatic triumphs to his more recent forays into comedy and villainy, Walken's versatility and commitment to his craft have left a uniquely special mark on cinema. Whether you're a longtime fan or a newcomer to his work, revisiting these films is a must for anyone who appreciates the art of acting and the enduring power of great performances.
